肥.meaning: A lazy farmer drags his <part>bed</part> out into the cabbage patch and sleeps there, snoring under the <part>moon</part>. His cows wander round him every night, and by spring the cabbages are the size of armchairs. Cow pats make great <kanji>fertilizer</kanji>.
肥.on: One morning he hops out of bed and his <sound>hee</sound>l sinks right into it.
肥.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala naps on a giant cabbage, and both keep getting fatter.

踏.meaning: The storm is over and the <part>sun</part> is out, so a kid in yellow boots marches down the street planting one <part>foot</part> in every puddle of <part>water</part>: splash, splash, splash. The postman gets soaked, the cat flees. She never skips a single puddle, not one <kanji>step</kanji>.
踏.on: At the deepest puddle her boot fills up, and cold water squishes round every <sound>toe</sound>.
踏.kun: Back home, she flops onto a <sound>fu</sound>ton by the fire to dry her socks.

紀.meaning: A wise <part>cobra</part> keeps the village's history by tying a knot in a long <part>thread</part> for every big event: a flood, a wedding, the day the goat ate the mayor's hat. Coiled in its basket, the thread is now miles long. Each knot is a line in the town's <kanji>chronicle</kanji>.
紀.on: The basket is locked with a brass <sound>key</sound> that the cobra keeps under its tongue.

酔.meaning: A miner lights a stick of <part>dynamite</part> beside the <part>signpost</part> at the crossroads. Boom: its arms spin and point every which way, up, down and sideways, and the post sways and hiccups. It looks completely <kanji>drunk</kanji>.
酔.on: Travellers argue about which arm points to the <sound>swee</sound>t shop.
酔.kun: A dizzy hiker leans on it, feeling sick, and spills <sound>yo</sound>gurt down his front.

沿.meaning: A lost duckling can't find the pond, so it trails the <part>water drops</part> leaking from a <part>funnel</part> strapped to a farmer's tractor. Drip, waddle, drip, waddle, across three fields and a car park. It has learned to <kanji>follow along</kanji>.
沿.on: The tractor's <sound>en</sound>gine puffs out smoke rings to keep it on track.
沿.kun: At the end of the trail, it flops onto a <sound>so</sound>fa beside the farmer.

州.meaning: Along a winding <part>river</part>, three lords each light a beacon fire on the bank, one bright <part>dot</part> between every pair of streams. Each fire marks a border; each lord hoists his own flag, mints his own coins and bans the others' cheese. Every glow is a separate <kanji>state</kanji>.
州.on: To cross a border, a traveller must take off one <sound>shoe</sound> and hand it to the guard as a toll.
州.kun: The lords meet only on a <sound>soo</sound>ty strip of sand in the river, black from the beacons: a sandbank.

欧.meaning: A tour guide drags her group through every <part>ward</part> of every old city on the map: ten countries in ten days, cathedral, museum, castle, repeat. On day nine the whole bus lets out one giant <part>yawn</part>. That's a coach trip round <kanji>Europe</kanji>.
欧.on: They nap under a huge <sound>oa</sound>k in the last town square.
欧.kun: The guide slurps <sound>u</sound>don, climbs into a fountain <sound>tu</sound>b and belts out a tune to wake them: to sing.
